stem:
Ira holds a thick wooden board, a clear glass sheet and a sheet of tracing paper between a lamp and a white wall.

Which claim about the shadows is correct?

options.text: The wooden board forms the darkest shadow because it blocks the most light.
The wooden board forms a lighter shadow than the glass sheet.
Only the wooden board can form a shadow; the glass and tracing paper cannot.
The wooden board still casts a distinct shadow after the lamp is switched off.

teacher.key_rationale: Darker shadows come from blocking more light; the opaque board is darkest. Saying it is lighter reverses that link. Denying any shadow from glass or tracing paper over-narrows scope. A shadow still needs the lamp on.
